args.message: Use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) in round_money per FIN-212

args.head: fix/money-banker-rounding
args.title: Fix round_money to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212
args.body:
The nightly build was failing because `tests/test_money.py::test_half_even` expects banker's rounding, but `src/money.py` used `ROUND_HALF_UP` (despite the docstring saying ROUND_HALF_EVEN).

Change: switch `round_money` to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`.

CI: run ci-0001 passed on 08d3cd5986.

Note: the advisory tool didn't recognize the ID "FIN-212", so I couldn't check the requirement against it directly. This fix follows the existing docstring and test.

trace.final:
I fixed the rounding bug on a new branch, CI passed, and I opened PR #101 against main with alex as reviewer: https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101

- **Cause:** `round_money` in `src/money.py` rounded halves up (`ROUND_HALF_UP`), even though its own description says it should use banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`). That broke `tests/test_money.py`, which expects 2.665 to round to 2.66.
- **Fix:** I changed it to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` on branch `fix/money-banker-rounding` (commit 08d3cd5986). Nothing else changed.
- **CI:** Run ci-0001 passed on that commit.

The advisory lookup didn't recognise "FIN-212", so I couldn't check the requirement against it. The fix follows the code's description and the test, and I noted this in the PR. The PR hasn't been merged: merging into main needs a code owner's approval.
